design_rationale:
TASK 0 DOSSIER (round 4) — start-up return into a carousel whose newest item ran empty between visits.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to return two unused flap discs for credit, a write she enters herself. The agent must read in the start-up return policy that a return of the item most recently added, against its latest vend, is not credited until its selection carries the start-up review par change Corbett owes for its stockout between scheduled visits; find from the selection history that AB-53318 (add entry VPC-517641, 2026-08-26) is that item, from the machine log that it ran empty on 2026-10-01 (5 units at the 2026-10-01 visit, above the 20 percent trigger of par 24, then vends of 2 and 3) and that no Corbett entry exists; size the par (6 factors over vends, StockSmart bins, credit ledger, contract lines, order lines) and record it; then figure the unit credit (4 factors) from the price paid on the world where that par stands.
SCOPE: draw {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "factor_counts": [4, 6]}; claims vending_ext_startup_par_review (6 factors, resize_selection_par_58ce1bb4, agent) and vending_ext_startup_item_return (4 factors, return_startup_item_units_bfc1c22c, user). Both writes (vending_selection_set, vending_item_returned) have empty base triggers.
PROBLEM TREE: root vending_ext_startup_item_return <- vending_ext_startup_par_review, value_input, gate fill_tier, form state. Prerequisite sentence: "A return of a start-up item is not credited until the item's selection carries the start-up review par change entry from Corbett that its stockout between scheduled restock visits owes." Ordering connective 'not ... until'; record-visible state; no tool, id or code token; exactly one writer (the par review's Corbett par change). Edge effect on this world: opening par 24 with ledger 24 = overstock handling charge; after the review's par 28, 24 >= 22.4 = near-full credit share. Skip run: unit credit 5.62 instead of 6.00.
FACTOR CARD par review (expected 28, baseline 20): demand_pattern_basis (method) largest single vend 6 (VT-5514861, 2026-09-03) >= average 45/40*7/2 = 3.9375 -> interval usage 6 (baseline 19); category_wear_allowance abrasives 0.25 (-> 23); storeroom_bin_backup bin A-03-12 not critical -> 0.85 (-> 33); consigned_exposure_limit one returned payment in 12 months (2026-03-17; 2025-09-08 is 12 whole months back) -> 0.8 (-> 35); supply_lead_allowance substitute line PCH-552311 and no removal line for AB-53318 -> 0.25 (-> 23); order_channel_share 10 units to ST-51842 < 45 -> 0.9 (-> 31). Par = ceil(6 x 1.5 x 0.85 x 0.8 x 0.9 / 0.2) = ceil(27.54) = 28, rounded up to a whole unit.
FACTOR CARD return (expected 6.00, baseline 6.85): price = the unit price of the item's latest vend VT-5515953 (highest vend number), the price paid, 6.85; today's competitive-match price 6.55 (PCH-552790) is a near-miss the rule does not use. fill_level_shape (method) ledger 69 - 45 = 24 vs par 28 -> near-full 6.85 x 0.95 = 6.5075 (baseline plain -> 6.32); trial_length_share 40 days -> 0.97 (-> 6.19); machine_return_rate one return line in 3 months (VR-5514207) -> 0.98 (-> 6.12); item_handling_share abrasives -> 0.97 (-> 6.19). Credit = RND(6.5075 x 0.97 x 0.98 x 0.97, 2) = RND(6.000447) = 6.00, rounded half up to the cent only at the end; line credit 2 x 6.00 = 12.00, below the 20.55 paid for the 3 units vended. No figure sits on a half cent.
METHOD PAIRWISE (fill_level_shape): overstock MX(0, p - 0.75) vs near-full 0.95p vs plain p; at p = 6.85: 6.10 / 6.5075 / 6.85.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: vending_selection_set under vending_planogram_management (Corbett changes not counted). vending_item_returned under vending_evt_returns_and_errors: return_inside_window (vend 2026-10-01, day 4 of 14; temporal_feasibility entry), one_credit_per_vend (VT-5515953 never returned or credited), same badge 57769, 2 <= 3 units. The overwrite scopes start-up returns against the newest item's latest vend; every other return stays at its vend price (VR-5514207 of SF-51207 credited at 9.85).
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: bay B-14 / AB-53318 on VP-551273; returned vend VT-5515953 (badge 57769, 3 units, 2026-10-01 10:28); decoys VT-5515942 (badge 57716, same morning, 2 units) and VT-5515837 (badge 57769, 2026-09-28, 1 unit).

user_scenario: You are Elena Vashti, purchasing and maintenance planner at Tamarack Gear Works, Inc., a gear and shaft machining shop in Warren, Michigan. You call Corbett Customer Care on Monday morning about the VendPoint carousel machine at the Plant 1 Machining Cell. One of your machinists, badge 57769, took three flap discs from the machine last Thursday morning, used only one, and still has the other two sealed in their original package. What you want is to return those two unused discs into the machine for credit today. You know a return into the machine is something the customer records itself, and you are ready to enter it yourself as long as the agent tells you exactly what to enter; you are not calling to change anything else on the machine and you have no other request. You speak plainly and keep to the point. When the agent asks you to identify the account you give the account number C-547218 and the bill-to ZIP 48093; only if a third detail is needed do you give the main phone number 2487316642. If the agent asks which machine, you read it off the front plate: serial VP-551273, the carousel machine in the Plant 1 Machining Cell, ship-to ST-51842. The discs came from bay B-14 and the item number on the package is AB-53318. You do not have the vend transaction number, and you do not know stocking levels or how Corbett prices things; if asked you say the agent should go by Corbett's records. Whatever the agent says Corbett has to do on its own side, you let them go ahead without questions. When the agent hands the return over for you to enter and gives you the values, you enter it with exactly those values and read back the reference and the credit it gives you. Once you hear that the return is in and what it credits, you thank the agent and end the call.
